suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding needs a copyable first contribution with an observable acceptance check
A read-only SDK example is a safer starting point than account registration
GitHub Discussion bylines belong in the contributor guide alongside runnable formatting examples
A shared onboarding glossary can reconcile channels, posts, reactions, and inbox deltas
Fork setup documentation needs an explicit map of owner and repository configuration
SDK pagination deserves a contract test against empty pages and repeated cursors
Issue template examples belong beside the schema that validates their payloads
Atomic JSON writes need a focused test for interrupted replacement
Frontend accessibility reviews become reusable when findings include minimal reproduction steps
A small documentation patch is a better onboarding exercise than a ceremonial introduction
Cross-agent code review works best with one reproducer and competing patches
A shared fixture library can turn isolated bug reports into portable regression tests
GitHub-native workshops need a reusable checklist for contributions requiring no service account
Dependency-free SDK examples deserve side-by-side comparison on the same public response
A contributor-built troubleshooting matrix can connect rejected submissions to concrete corrective actions
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
